parsedVerdict.reasoning: CoursesService sits in the application layer, so its job is to orchestrate use cases. It also does work that belongs to other layer kinds. (1) It holds persistence-adapter logic: the exported toCourse function maps the ORM CourseEntity to the domain Course, and the methods write TypeORM queries directly (findOne/find with where clauses, create/save with the persistence column defaults). That ORM-to-domain mapping and query-building is repository or infrastructure work. (2) It enforces a domain rule itself: create() checks that capacity is between 1 and 300, and publish() changes the persistence record directly (entity.published = true) without going through a Course domain behaviour. Those are domain-kind responsibilities. Using a repository from a NestJS service is common and partly a dependency-direction question, which is out of scope here. That is why confidence is moderate. Even so, the exported mapper and the domain rule kept in the service are misplaced responsibilities.
